chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Dawud ibn Abdillah, from Amr ibn Muhammad, from Isa ibn Yunus who said:

Ibn Abi al-Awja' said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) during one of his dialogues with him: 'You have mentioned God, and thus referred to an absent [entity].' So Abu Abdillah said: 'Woe to you! How can He who is present with His creation as a witness be absent, and closer to them than the jugular vein — He hears their speech, sees their persons, and knows their secrets?'
So Ibn Abi al-Awja' said: 'Is He in every place? Is it not that if He were in the sky, how could He be in the earth, and if He were in the earth, how could He be in the sky?'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, you have described a created being who, when it moves from a place, a place becomes occupied by it and a place becomes empty of it, so it does not know, while it is in the place it came to be in, what is occurring in the place it was in. But as for God, the Magnificent of Glory, the King, the Judge — no place is ever empty of Him, no place is ever occupied by Him, and He is no closer to any place than to another place.'

key_terms.الْمَخْلُوق: The created being — used to contrast spatial constraints of creation with God's transcendence
key_terms.الْمَلِكُ الدَّيَّان: The King, the Judge — Divine titles affirming sovereignty and justice beyond spatial constraints
key_terms.حَبْلُ الْوَرِيد: The jugular vein — Quranic expression (Q 50:16) denoting intimate proximity
key_terms.شَاهِد: Present as witness — counter-attribute affirming God's omnipresence with His creation
key_terms.غَائِب: Absent/hidden — the freethinker's characterization of God as spatially absent and therefore inaccessible

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq respond to the claim that God is absent or hidden?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) engages in a theological debate with Ibn Abi al-Awja', a well-known dualist and freethinker of 2nd-century Basra who challenged the existence of God by claiming He was 'absent.' The Imam refutes this with a Quranic allusion (closer than the jugular vein, Q 50:16), asserting God's omnipresence and omniscience. He then dismantles Ibn Abi al-Awja''s spatial argument by explaining that spatial limitations apply only to created beings who are constrained by place, whereas God transcends space entirely — He neither vacates any place nor is contained within any place, making the concept of spatial location inapplicable to the Divine.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Dawood Bin Abdullah, from Amro Bin Muhammad, from Isa Bin Yunus who said,

‘Ibn Abu Al-Awja’a said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in what was one of his dialogues with him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> mentioned Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so you<sup>asws</sup> referred to a Hidden’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you<sup>asws</sup>! How can He<sup>azwj</sup> happen to be hidden, the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who is with His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures as a Witness, and is closer to them than the jugular vein? He<sup>azwj</sup> Hears their speech and Sees their persons, and Knows their secrets?’

So Ibn Abu Al-Awja’a said, ‘Is He<sup>azwj</sup> is in every place? Is it not so that if He<sup>azwj</sup> was in the sky, how could He<sup>azwj</sup> happen to be in the earth, and when He<sup>azwj</sup> was in the earth, how could He<sup>azwj</sup> happen to be in the sky?’

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, you are describing the created being who, when he transfers from a place, a place is occupied by him and a space is empty from him, so he does not know (when he) is in the place in which he came to be in, what occurs in the place which he was in. But, as for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Magnificent of Glory, the King, the Judge. So, neither is a place empty from Him<sup>azwj</sup> nor is a space occupied by Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor does He<sup>azwj</sup> happen to be nearer to a place than to a (another) place’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (the narrator of the above Hadith) from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Dawud ibn ‘Abdallah from ‘Amr ibn Muhammad from ‘Isa ibn Yunus who has said the following.

“Ibn abu al-‘Awja said to Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) in one of their conversations, ‘You spoke of Allah and referred to an unseen.’” The Imam (a.s.) said, “What you said is not proper. How would He be unseen when He is present with His creatures and is closer to them than their jugular vein. He hears their speeches, sees their persons and knows their secrets.”
Ibn abu al-‘Awja then said, “Is He everywhere? If He is in the heavens, how can He, at the same time, be on earth and when He would be on earth then how can He be in the heavens at the same time.?”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “You spoke only of a creature that with changing place any other place becomes occupied with it and another place is vacated from him and does not know what has happened to the place where he used to be. Allah’s position is great. He is the king Who has full account of all things. No place is without Him and He does not occupy any place. He is nearer to one place than the other place.”
